# Tools and code

This page describes how a workflow calls HTTP APIs and runs Python. Read [workflow-format.md](workflow-format.md) first.

Statements marked "verified in a working builder" come from a builder that created a 6-node workflow through the REST API. The workflow has code nodes, `api_call` tools, post-hooks and transitions on tool results. Its agent passed its practice cases. Statements marked "seen in a trial call" come from the event log of a simulation call made with that builder.

## Tool function shape

Every external action is a **tool function**. The shape is the same wherever you attach it.

```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
  "function": {
    "name": "lookup_order",
    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
    "description": "Look up one order. CALL it when the caller asks about a specific order.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/orders/lookup" },
        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
        "headers": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } }
        },
        "body": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "customer_id": { "type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}" },
            "order_number": { "type": "string", "description": "Order number, digits only", "default": "{{order_number}}" }
          },
          "required": ["order_number"]
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | Always `"function"` |
| `function.name` | Tool name. The model calls it by this name. Result variables are named after it |
| `function.handler` | Which runtime executes the tool. See the table below |
| `function.description` | Read by the dialogue model when the tool is in `tools`. Ignored in `pre_actions` |
| `function.parameters` | JSON-schema object. `properties` holds the parameters |
| `config.timeoutMs` | Timeout of one attempt, in milliseconds |
| `config.maxRetries` | Tool-level retries of a failed call |
| `config.interruptible` | `false` makes the tool run in the background. See "Background tools" |
| `config.alwaysRunsAt` | Makes the tool a lifecycle tool. See "Lifecycle tools" |
| `response_mapping` | Tool level, for tools in `tools`. Maps the result to variables |
| `pre_process_code` | Python hook that runs before the call |
| `post_process_code` | Python hook that runs after the call |

| Handler | Runs |
|---|---|
| `__function__:api_call` | An HTTP request |
| `__function__:code_exec` | A Python snippet in a sandbox |
| `__function__:end_call` | Hangs up. Used in the `terminal` of an `end_call` node |

Handlers for integrations, knowledge search, call transfer and rescheduling also exist. They are not needed here.

`api_call` parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `url` | Request URL. `{{var}}` works |
| `method` | HTTP method |
| `headers` | Object. Each header is a property with a `default` |
| `body` | Object. Each body field is a property under `body.properties` |
| `connect_retries` | Transport retries. See "Retries and timeouts" |

## How a parameter gets its value

One key decides, per parameter: `default`.

| Declaration | Who supplies the value | Does the model see the parameter |
|---|---|---|
| `default` with a literal, or with a `{{var}}` that has a value | The workflow. The value is **baked** | No |
| `default` with a `{{var}}` that has no value when the node is entered | The model | Yes, named after the variable, with the property's `type`, `description` and `enum` |
| no `default` | The model | Yes |
| `const` | Nobody. `const` does **not** bake | It only constrains the model's own output |

Rules:

- **Use `default` for fixed backend config** such as `url`, `method` and auth headers. At registration the engine moves every `default` into the tool's base config, resolves `{{var}}` from the variable table, and removes the field from the schema the model sees.
- **Never use `const` for a value you want sent.** The engine reads only `default`. A `{{var}}` inside a `const` never resolves. An `api_call` whose `url` is a `const` fails with "URL is required".
- **Baking happens when the node is entered.** A `{{var}}` default is resolved against the variable table at that moment.

The working builder uses this for every tool: `customer_id` has `"default": "{{customer_id}}"` and is baked from a call variable. Every other body field has `"default": "{{<field name>}}"`, where no variable of that name exists, so the model fills it. Verified in a working builder.

Seen in a trial call: the model's arguments are stored as `<tool>_args.<field>` in the variable table, for example `lookup_order_args.order_number`. They were not stored under the bare field name.

Take care that a model-filled field does not share its name with a variable that is already set when the node is entered. The value would be baked and the model would never see the parameter.

### `api_call` body field rules

- Declare each body field as a leaf under `body.properties.<field>`.
- Put the field's `type`, `description` and `enum` on that leaf. Put required fields in `body.required`.
- Give each leaf its own `default`.
- Do not put a field spec at the top level of `parameters.properties` next to a `body.default` template object. The engine looks for the spec at `body.properties.<field>`, does not find it, and the model sees only "Template variable: name". The `enum` and `description` are lost while the call still works.
- A body that exists only as one `body.default` object also shows as an empty form in the dashboard editor. Saving from there removes the tool.

A `code_exec` tool is different: its parameters are true top-level arguments. Declare a model-filled one as a top-level property without `default`.

### When a baked variable has no value

| Field type | Variable unset | Variable is `""` |
|---|---|---|
| Normal field in an engine-run call (`pre_actions`, lifecycle tool) | The field is dropped from the request. No error | The field is sent empty |
| `code` of `code_exec` | The literal text `{{var}}` stays in the Python source and the snippet crashes | |

Fix: make sure an earlier node always sets the variable, even to a sentinel value. In code, read variables from `vars` and do not splice them in with `{{var}}`.

### Constrain model-filled parameters

When a value must be one of a known set, do not use a free string. The model sometimes invents a value that looks plausible.

- Use an `enum` on the leaf, and list the values in the `description` as well.
- Or use a `number` that is an index into a list, with the valid range in the description. A pre-hook or the backend turns the index into the real value.
- If neither is possible, name the exact source in the description and tell the model to copy the value unchanged.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "queue": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Team that takes over. One of: billing, delivery, returns.",
      "enum": ["billing", "delivery", "returns"],
      "default": "{{queue}}"
    }
  },
  "required": ["queue"]
}
```

## `pre_actions` versus `tools`

The placement decides who fires the call.

| Placement | Node type | Who calls it | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pre_actions` | `api_request`, `code` | The engine | On node entry, before any model turn |
| `tools` | `conversation` | The dialogue model | During a turn, when the model decides to |
| Workflow-level `tools` with `config.alwaysRunsAt` | none | The engine | At call start or call end |

The platform removes `tools` from non-conversation nodes and `pre_actions` from conversation nodes. It does so without an error: the JSON you sent looks fine, the create call succeeds, and the stored node has an empty array. A node cannot use both.

**Use `pre_actions`** when the call must always run and the model has nothing to decide. Example: after the order number is known, always fetch the order.

**Use `tools`** when the call depends on what the user says. Example: cancel the order only if the caller asks for it.

Differences in behaviour:

| | `pre_actions` | `tools` |
|---|---|---|
| Can be skipped | No | Yes. The model may not call it if the description and the prompt do not push for it |
| Timing | Node entry | Inside a turn. The model can call a tool, speak, then call another |
| Result in the conversation | A tool call and tool result pair is added to the history | The same |
| `response_mapping` lives | On the **node** | On the **tool** |
| `description` | Ignored | The only text the model reads about the tool |

To run a fixed call before a tool-driven conversation, use a passthrough `api_request` node and transition from it into the conversation node. Do not build a long chain of passthrough nodes for optional actions. Put those into one conversation node with several tools.

### A `pre_actions` node

```json
{
  "name": "fetch_order",
  "node_type": "api_request",
  "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "present",
  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
  "pre_actions": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
      "function": {
        "name": "get_order",
        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
        "description": "Get the order.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/get_order" },
            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
            "headers": { "type": "object", "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } } },
            "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_number": { "type": "string", "default": "{{order_number}}" } }, "required": [] }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
  ],
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "present", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

The last `always` transition is mandatory. A passthrough node with no matching transition deadlocks.

### Tool descriptions

In `tools`, the `description` decides whether the model calls the tool.

- Write it as an instruction with the trigger: "CALL it every time the caller gives an order number."
- A plain description such as "Looks up an order" lets the model acknowledge the request in words and never call the tool. That is the most common failure of nodes with many tools.
- If two tools could match, say which one not to use and name the other.
- In `task_message`, put the tool rules before long reference text and state: when a rule says to use a tool, call the tool.
- The working builder also tells the model to call one tool per message and to speak after every tool result. Verified in a working builder. In a trial call a model turn with no text and no tool call produced the error event "The model returned no speakable content".

A tool is available only in the nodes that list it. Seen in a trial call: the model called a tool that the current node did not list. The result was the text "The function `<name>` is not currently available."

## `response_mapping`

`response_mapping` copies values from a call result into named variables. It needs no model call.

```json
{
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" },
    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | Dot path into the tool result |
| `variable` | Name of the variable to set |

### Placement

- For a tool in `tools`: inside the tool object, next to `function` and `config`.
- For `pre_actions`: at the **node level**. A `response_mapping` nested inside a `pre_actions` entry is ignored and the variable never appears.

`extraction_schema` follows the same placement rule if you use it on a call result.

### Where a result lands (trial findings)

Seen in a trial call: the result of an `api_call` is an envelope around the HTTP response.

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": { "ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3 },
  "message": "Successfully executed POST request",
  "status_code": 200,
  "header": { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
}
```

`data` is the JSON body the API returned. `header` holds the HTTP response headers.

The engine also writes every result into the variable table by itself, flattened with dots. You do not need a mapping for these. For a tool named `check_answer` whose API returned `{"ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3}`, the trial call's variable table held:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `check_answer_args.<field>` | Each argument the model sent |
| `check_answer_response.status` | `success` |
| `check_answer_response.data.ok` | `true` (a string) |
| `check_answer_response.data.verified` | `true` (a string) |
| `check_answer_response.data.attempts_left` | `3` |
| `check_answer_response.message` | `Successfully executed POST request` |
| `check_answer_response.status_code` | `200` |
| `check_answer_response.header.<Header-Name>` | One variable per response header |
| `check_answer_status_code` | `200` |
| `check_answer_success_count` | Number of successful calls so far |

Each call of the same tool overwrites the previous `_args` and `_response` values.

### Which mapping paths work

- **Start the path at the envelope, with `data.`**. If the API returns `{"ok": true}`, map `data.ok`. If it returns `{"products": [...]}`, map `data.products`. Verified in a working builder, on a tool-level mapping and on a node-level mapping.
- A path without the `data.` prefix (for the same body: `ok`) is not confirmed. A smaller example builder uses it. In an early trial call the mapped variables stayed unset and the transitions on them never fired. The mapping paths of that call are not recorded. The builder that passed uses `data.` paths.
- The flattened key can be used directly as a transition variable: `check_answer_response.data.verified`. Verified in a working builder, which tests the mapped variable and the flattened key in the same OR group as a safeguard.
- Booleans arrive as strings. The trial call showed `true` in lower case in the flattened keys. Test both `"true"` and `"True"`, or map a string field.
- A mapped list or object: the exact form it has later inside `vars` is not confirmed. The working builder reads it defensively. It accepts a list, a JSON string, and flattened keys.

## Routing on tool results

Routing runs again after a tool result arrives. A transition on a result variable fires in the same turn, before any further model turn. Seen in a trial call.

```json
{
  "transitions": [
    {
      "target_node": "load_order",
      "description": "The check passed",
      "condition": {
        "logic": "or",
        "conditions": [
          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" },
          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- On a passthrough node, end with an `always` transition so that a failed or empty response does not deadlock.
- Use a tool result to leave a conversation node. The pattern "a closing tool sets a variable, a transition on that variable leads to an `end_call` node" is verified in a working builder.
- To leave a node that carries out an action, do not re-test the user's earlier intent with `matches_intent`. The router looks at the latest user message and can route away before the tool was called. Extract a follow-up enum with a default such as `stay`, and branch with `equals`.

### Success and failure counters

The engine keeps two integer variables per call target. No mapping is needed.

| Placement | Variables |
|---|---|
| `pre_actions` node | `<nodeId>_success_count`, `<nodeId>_failure_count` |
| Tool in `tools` with handler `api_call` | `<toolName>_success_count`, `<toolName>_failure_count` |

Seen in a trial call: `check_answer_success_count` was `2` after two successful calls, and a code node named `setup` produced `setup_success_count` with the value `1`.

```json
{
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "give_up", "description": "The lookup failed three times", "condition": { "logic": "or", "conditions": [ { "variable": "lookup_order_failure_count", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 2 } ] } },
    { "target_node": "ask_again", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

### `suppress_tool_results`

A node-level boolean for nodes that run API calls. With `true` the dialogue model sees only a short `{status: "success"}` summary in place of the raw response. Variables are still mapped and routing still sees them. Use it for large responses, or when the mapped variables already hold everything the model needs.

### Background tools

A tool with `"config": {"interruptible": false}` runs in the background. A user interruption does not cancel it. Its result arrives one or more turns later. The mapped variables, the `_response` keys and the counters are filled as usual, but not in the same turn. A transition that reads them right after the call can find them unset. Gate on the variable with `is_set`.

## Retries and timeouts

| Setting | Where | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `timeoutMs` | `config` | not documented | Time limit of one attempt, in milliseconds |
| `maxRetries` | `config` | not documented | Tool-level retries after a failed response |
| `connect_retries` | `parameters.properties`, as a baked parameter | `2` | Retries when the connection could not be established |
| `timeout_ms` | `code_exec` parameter | `30000` | Time limit of a code snippet |

`connect_retries` in detail:

- It retries only failures to establish the connection: connection refused, or reset during the TCP or TLS handshake. The request never reached the server, so a repeat is safe even for POST.
- HTTP error statuses and timeouts are not retried by it.
- Hard cap `5`. `0` means a single attempt.
- Back-off is 150 ms times the attempt number, with a new connection each time.
- All attempts share one 30 second budget for the request.
- Declare it next to `url` and `method`: `"connect_retries": {"type": "number", "default": 0}`. It is not a `config` field.

The working builder sets `maxRetries` to `0` on tools that write data and to `2` on its read-only `pre_actions` call. A retried write can record the same thing twice if the API is not idempotent.

## Pre and post Python hooks

An `api_call` tool can carry two Python snippets. They run on the server, in a sandbox, right before and right after the call. They are top-level fields of the tool object.

```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 0 },
  "function": {
    "name": "check_answer",
    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
    "description": "Check one answer. CALL it every time the caller answers the question.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/check_answer" },
        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
        "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "answer": { "type": "string", "description": "The caller's answer", "default": "{{answer}}" } }, "required": ["answer"] }
      }
    }
  },
  "pre_process_code": "vars['member_code'] = str(vars.get('member_code') or '').strip().upper()",
  "post_process_code": "try:\n    if isinstance(result, dict):\n        result.pop('header', None)\n        d = result.get('data')\n        if isinstance(d, dict):\n            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Ask the next question.' if d.get('verified') else 'Ask the same question again.'\nexcept Exception:\n    pass\n"
}
```

| Hook | Names available | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `pre_process_code` | `vars`: mutable dict that fills the `{{var}}` placeholders of the request. `config`: the substituted request with `url`, `method`, `headers`, `body` | Clean a value, or rewrite the whole request |
| `post_process_code` | `result`: the tool result, mutable | Reshape, shorten or extend the result |

Documented behaviour:

- The post-hook runs before `response_mapping` and extraction see the result.
- An empty or whitespace-only string means no hook.
- Hooks are honoured only on `api_call` tools (and on the integration and knowledge search handlers). The platform removes them from any other handler when the workflow is saved.
- In a pre-hook, setting `config['body']` to a string sends that string as the raw body, with no JSON encoding. Set the `Content-Type` header yourself in that case.

### What `result` looks like in a post-hook

The internal reference shows `result` as the response body. A working builder shows otherwise. Verified in a working builder:

- For an `api_call`, `result` is the envelope described above: a dict with `status`, `data`, `message`, `status_code` and `header`. The API's JSON body is `result["data"]`.
- A key that the hook adds inside `result["data"]` reaches the dialogue model as part of the tool result. The working builder adds a `what_to_do_next` sentence there, and its prompt tells the model to obey it.
- `result.pop("header", None)` removes the response headers. The working builder does this on every tool, so that headers do not take up space in the model's context.
- Mapping paths still start with `data.` when a post-hook is present.

The working builder writes every hook inside `try` and `except Exception: pass` and checks types with `isinstance` before use. What the platform does when a hook raises is not documented.

Seen in a test on 10 October: a post-hook can read call variables and write new variables, and a later pre-hook reads them. Not confirmed: whether a change to `result` also changes the flattened `<tool>_response.*` variables.

## Code nodes and `code_exec`

A `code` node runs a Python snippet when it is entered. The snippet is a `code_exec` function in `pre_actions`.

```json
{
  "name": "compute_delivery",
  "node_type": "code",
  "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "tell_delivery",
  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
  "pre_actions": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "code_exec",
        "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "code": { "type": "string", "default": "import datetime\ntry:\n    start = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('shipped_on'))[:10])\n    eta = start + datetime.timedelta(days=3)\n    vars['delivery_day'] = eta.isoformat()\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'known'\nexcept Exception:\n    vars['delivery_day'] = ''\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'unknown'\n" },
            "timeout_ms": { "type": "number", "default": 10000 }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "tell_delivery", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `code` | The Python source, as a baked `default` string |
| `timeout_ms` | Time limit in milliseconds. Default `30000` |

### Reading and writing variables

- The snippet gets a dict named `vars`. It holds the current workflow variables.
- Read with `vars.get("name")`. A variable that was never set is absent.
- Write with `vars["name"] = value`. Every key the snippet assigns becomes a workflow variable.

Verified in a working builder:

- Call variables are in `vars`. The builder reads `vars.get("now")`, a call variable passed with the simulation.
- The result of an earlier `api_request` node is reachable from `vars` in a later code node. The builder looks for it under the mapped variable name first and under the flattened result keys second. Which of the two held the data is not recorded.
- A string written to `vars["date_facts"]` in a code node resolves as `{{date_facts}}` in the `task_message` of later conversation nodes. Multi-line strings work.
- The standard modules `json`, `re` and `datetime` can be imported.
- The same snippet can run in two code nodes at different points of the call. The later run sees the variables added in between.

### What a code node returns

Seen in a trial call: the result of a successful `code_exec` is

```json
{ "status": "success", "data": null, "message": "Code executed successfully", "status_code": 200 }
```

The snippet's output is not in `data`. Its values reach the workflow only through `vars`. After a code node named `setup` ran, the variable table held:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| each key the snippet wrote, for example `date_facts` | the value, with source `tool_result` and source node `setup` |
| `setup_response.status` | `success` |
| `setup_response.data` | `null` |
| `setup_response.message` | `Code executed successfully` |
| `setup_response.status_code` | `200` |
| `setup_status_code` | `200` |
| `setup_success_count` | `1` |

For a code node the automatic keys are named after the **node**, not after `code_exec`.

### Rules for snippets

- **Do not write `{{` or `}}` in the code.** The internal sources disagree on whether the `code` field is templated. One says it is exempt. Another says placeholders are resolved when the code runs and an unset one is left as literal text, which breaks the Python. The working builder removes every `{{` and `}}` from generated code (a nested dict literal such as `{'a': {'b': 1}}` ends in `}}`) and reads all values from `vars`.
- **Never let a snippet raise.** Wrap the body in `try` and `except`, and write a fallback value for every variable that a later prompt or condition reads. A prompt that references an unset variable shows the literal placeholder to the model.
- **Write strings for routing flags**, such as `known` and `unknown`. Do not route on a Python boolean. See "Do not route on a boolean" in workflow-format.md.
- Keep snippets fast. They block the conversation.
- Do arithmetic, date calculation and counting in code, and give the model the finished facts as text. Verified in a working builder: it computes a block of date facts in a code node and places it in the prompts.
- Treat a code node like an API node: `passthrough: true`, a `passthrough_default_transition`, and a last `always` transition.

### Sandbox limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Time | `timeout_ms`, default `30000` |
| Modules | `json`, `re` and `datetime` are verified in a working builder. The full list is not documented |
| Network and file access | Not documented |
| Memory and output size | Not documented |

### `code_exec` as a tool

`code_exec` can also be a tool in the `tools` array of a conversation node, called by the model. Its parameters are top-level arguments, declared without `default` so the model fills them. For such a tool the `code` field resolves `{{var}}` when the tool is called, against the current variable table. The working builder does not use this form, so nothing about it is verified here.

## Lifecycle tools

A tool whose `config.alwaysRunsAt` is a non-empty list is never shown to the model. The engine fires it at a fixed point of the call.

| Value | When |
|---|---|
| `start_of_call` | During call setup, before the first turn |
| `end_of_call` | After the call has ended |
| `each_turn` | Accepted by the schema but not implemented. It never fires |

Put a lifecycle tool that must run on every call into the workflow's top-level `tools` array.

```json
{
  "initial_node": "greeting",
  "nodes": {},
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "config": { "alwaysRunsAt": ["end_of_call"] },
      "function": {
        "name": "push_call_result",
        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/call-results" },
            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
            "body": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "summary": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.analysis.summary}}" },
                "reason": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.call_end_reason}}" }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- A workflow-level tool without `alwaysRunsAt` never runs and the model never sees it.
- A lifecycle tool in a node's `tools` runs for `start_of_call` only on the `initial_node`, and for `end_of_call` only on the node in which the call ended.
- If a `{{var}}` parameter is still unresolved, one model call fills the parameters. If everything resolves, the handler runs directly.
- `response_mapping` is applied for `start_of_call`. It is not applied for `end_of_call`.
- At the end of a call the order is: call analysis, then `end_of_call` tools, then success-criteria judging. An `end_of_call` tool can use `{{call.analysis.summary}}`, `{{call.analysis.structured_data_str}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason_category}}`, `{{call.call_tags}}` and `{{call.duration}}`.
- A malformed lifecycle tool is dropped at run time without an error. Validate with a dry run (api.md).

## Tool results and the next turn

After a tool call returns, the model sees the result and has to produce the next turn itself. Two things were seen in practice runs with the hackathon's agent model:

- **The agent says nothing after the tool call.** The result arrives, no assistant message follows, and the simulated customer hangs up after waiting. It happens more often when the result is bare data such as `{"ok": true, "verified": true}`.
- **The agent ignores a negative result.** For example it reads `"verified": false` and moves on to the next question as if the answer had passed.

What fixed both in a working builder (verified, see the post-hook section above): a post-hook on the tool that adds one plain instruction line to the result before the model sees it, for example a `what_to_do_next` field that says what the answer means and what to say or call next. The model then has something to act on.

Also say it in the step's prompt: after every tool result, speak to the customer or call the next tool. Never end a turn with nothing.

## Checklist

- Fixed values use `default`, never `const`.
- Each `api_call` body field is a leaf under `body.properties` with its own `default`, `description` and `enum`.
- `tools` only on `conversation` nodes. `pre_actions` only on `api_request` and `code` nodes.
- `response_mapping` on the tool for `tools`, on the node for `pre_actions`.
- Mapping paths start with `data.`.
- Booleans from results are tested as `"true"` and `"True"`, or replaced by string fields.
- Every passthrough node ends with an `always` transition.
- Code reads and writes through `vars`, never raises, and contains no `{{` or `}}`.
- Tool descriptions say when to call the tool.

COMPOSE = r'''

    f = num((blk or dict()).get('remainingDebt'))

        if str(c.get('cardNumber')) == arg:

        sel = str(match[0].get('cardNumber'))

        sel = arg or str(v.get('sel_card') or '')
    v['sel_card'] = sel
    try:
        rc = json.loads(v.get('read_cards') or '[]')
    except Exception:
        rc = []
    if sel not in rc:
        rc.append(sel)
    v['read_cards'] = json.dumps(rc)
    nm = clean_name(d.get('productName'))
    v['sel_name'] = nm
    v['sel_last4'] = last4
    base = 'Sonu ' + digits(last4) + ' ile biten ' + (nm + ' ' if nm else '') + 'kartınız'
    v['sel_card_phrase'] = base
    stmt = pdate(d.get('statementDate'))
    due = pdate(d.get('lastPayDate'))
    ncut = pdate(d.get('nextStatementDate'))
    v['stmt_date_raw'] = str(d.get('statementDate') or '')
    t = today()
    present = [c for c in CUR if isinstance(d.get(c[1]), dict)]
    out = []
    kind = 'normal'
    if not stmt:
        kind = 'nodebt'
        out.append(base + 'ın henüz kesilmiş bir ekstresi olmadığı için ekstre borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.')
        if ncut:
            out.append('İlk hesap kesim tarihiniz ' + sdate(ncut) + ' olacak.')
    elif (t and ncut and t == ncut) or (t and due and t > due):
        if t == ncut:
            out.append('Hesap kesim tarihiniz bugün, ekstreniz saat 00.00 itibarıyla kesilecek.')
        else:
            out.append('Son ödeme tarihiniz olan ' + sdate(due) + ' geçti.')
        tots = []
        for c in present:
            f = num(d[c[1]].get('totalDebt'))
            if f is not None and f > 0:
                tots.append(c[2] + ' cinsinden toplam borcunuz ' + money(f, c[0]))
        if tots:
            out.append(base + 'a ait güncel toplam borcunuz şöyle: ' + ', '.join(tots) + '.')
        else:
            out.append(base + 'ın borcu bulunmamaktadır.')
        tl = d.get('debtTL') or dict()
        ra = num(tl.get('remainAutomaticPaymentAmount'))
        if t != ncut and str(d.get('automaticPaymentFlag')) == 'Y' and ra and ra > 0:
            out.append('Otomatik ödeme talimatınızdan tahsil edilecek kalan tutar ' + money(ra, 'TL') + '.')
    elif str(d.get('statementPaymentStatus')) == 'NO_DEBT' or not any(debt_of(d[c[1]]) for c in present):
        kind = 'nodebt'
        s = base + 'ın ' + sdate(stmt) + ' tarihli ekstresinden borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.'
        tl = d.get('debtTL') or dict()
        g = num(tl.get('totalDebt'))
        if g is not None and g > 0:
            s += ' Gelecek dönemler dahil toplam borcunuz ' + money(g, 'TL') + '.'
        if due:
            s += ' Son ödeme tarihiniz ' + sdate(due) + ' olacaktır.'
        out.append(s)
    else:

        clear = []
        for c in present:
            blk = d[c[1]]
            if not debt_of(blk):
                clear.append(c[2])
                continue
            sd = money(blk.get('statementDebt'), c[0])
            mp = money(blk.get('minPayment'), c[0])
            rd = money(blk.get('remainingDebt'), c[0])
            rmp_f = num(blk.get('remainingMinPayment')) or 0.0
            mp_f = num(blk.get('minPayment')) or 0.0
            rmp = money(blk.get('remainingMinPayment'), c[0])
            if c[0] == 'TL':
                if rmp_f > 0 and rmp_f >= mp_f:
                    s = 'Türk Lirası borcunuz ' + sd + ', ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ' + mp + '.'
                elif rmp_f <= 0:
                    s = 'Türk Lirası borcunuz ' + sd + ', kalan toplam borcunuz ' + rd + '. Minimum ödemenizi yaptığınız için teşekkür ederiz.'
                else:
                    s = 'Türk Lirası borcunuz ' + sd + ', ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ' + mp + ', kalan toplam borcunuz ' + rd + ', kalan minimum ödeme tutarınız ' + rmp + '.'
            else:
                s = c[2] + ' borcunuz ' + sd + ', kalan toplam borcunuz ' + rd + ', ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ' + mp + '.'
            if first:
                s = opening + s
                first = False
            out.append(s)
        if clear:
            if len(clear) == 1:
                out.append(clear[0] + ' borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.')
            else:
                out.append(', '.join(clear[:-1]) + ' ve ' + clear[-1] + ' borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.')
        if due:
            if t and t == due:
                out.append('Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz bugündür.')
            else:
                out.append('Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz ' + sdate(due) + "'" + cop(due) + '.')

        vv['code_error'] = str(e)
    except Exception:
        pass
'''

{extra}
        except Exception:
            pass
        msg = {ok_msg!r} if ok else {err_msg!r}

    if enum:
        f['enum'] = enum

def api_fn(name, service, body, desc, ok_msg, err_msg, extra='', retries=0, timeout=15000):
    return {
        'type': 'function',
        'config': {'timeoutMs': timeout, 'maxRetries': retries},
        'function': {
            'name': name,
            'handler': '__function__:api_call',
            'description': desc,
            'parameters': {
                'type': 'object',
                'properties': {
                    'url': {'type': 'string', 'default': MOCK + service},
                    'method': {'type': 'string', 'default': 'POST'},
                    'headers': {'type': 'object', 'properties': {
                        'Content-Type': {'type': 'string', 'default': 'application/json'},
                        'Accept': {'type': 'string', 'default': 'application/json'}}},
                    'body': {'type': 'object', 'properties': body, 'required': list(body.keys())},
                },
            },
        },
        'pre_process_code': PRE_HOOK,
        'post_process_code': post_hook(name, ok_msg, err_msg, extra),
    }


def code_node(name, src, transitions, x):
    full = COMMON + '\n' + src
    assert '{{' not in full and '}}' not in full, name
    return {
        'name': name, 'node_type': 'code', 'passthrough': True,
        'passthrough_default_transition': transitions[-1]['target_node'],
        'on_enter': {'type': 'silent'}, 'disable_inactivity_monitor': True,

                             'timeout_ms': {'type': 'number', 'default': 10000}}}}}],
        'transitions': transitions, 'position': {'x': x, 'y': 0},

        'passthrough_default_transition': transitions[-1]['target_node'],
        'on_enter': on_enter or {'type': 'silent'}, 'disable_inactivity_monitor': True,
        'pre_actions': [fn], 'transitions': transitions, 'position': {'x': x, 'y': 0},

{extra}

    return {
        'type': 'function',

    return {'logic': 'or', 'conditions': [{'variable': a, 'operator': 'equals', 'operand': b} for a, b in pairs]}


def tr(target, desc, cond):
    return {'target_node': target, 'description': desc, 'condition': cond}


ALWAYS = {'operator': 'always'}


def intent(d):
    return {'operator': 'matches_intent', 'description': d}


def end_node(name, fname, msg, x, y=400):
    return {
        'name': name, 'node_type': 'end_call', 'on_enter': {'type': 'silent'}, 'disable_inactivity_monitor': True,
        'transitions': [], 'position': {'x': x, 'y': y},
        'terminal': {'type': 'function', 'function': {'name': fname, 'handler': '__function__:end_call', 'parameters': {
            'type': 'object', 'properties': {'message_mode': {'type': 'string', 'default': 'custom'},
                                             'spoken_message': {'type': 'string', 'default': msg}}}}},
    }


NO_TOOL = ' Bu adımda hiçbir araç (tool) çağırma.'


def conv(name, task, x, on_enter=None, extraction=None, transitions=None, tools=None, max_turns=4, fail='end_tries', first_only=False, y=0):
    n = {'name': name, 'node_type': 'conversation', 'task_message': task,
         'on_enter': on_enter or {'type': 'llm'}, 'transitions': transitions or [],
         'max_node_turns': max_turns, 'max_turn_transition': fail, 'position': {'x': x, 'y': y}}
    if first_only:
        n['on_enter_first_entry_only'] = True
    if extraction:
        n['extraction_schema'] = extraction
    if tools:
        n['tools'] = tools
    return n


def ext(name, desc, enum=None, conf=0.6):
    e = {'name': name, 'type': 'string', 'description': desc, 'min_confidence': conf}
    if enum:
        e['enum_values'] = enum
    return e

def post_hook(name, ok_msg, err_msg, extra=''):
    return f"""import json
try:
    if isinstance(result, dict):
        result.pop('header', None)
        body = result.get('data')
        ok = isinstance(body, dict) and isinstance(body.get('data'), dict) and str((body.get('result') or dict()).get('returnCode')) == '1'
        code = ''
        if isinstance(body, dict) and isinstance(body.get('result'), dict):
            code = str(body['result'].get('code') or '')
        try:
            vv = vars
            if isinstance(vv, dict):
                vv['hk_{name}'] = json.dumps(body, ensure_ascii=False) if isinstance(body, dict) else ''
{extra}
        except Exception:
            pass
        msg = {ok_msg!r} if ok else {err_msg!r}
        if isinstance(body, dict):
            body['what_to_do_next'] = msg
        else:
            result['data'] = dict(what_to_do_next=msg)
except Exception:
    pass
"""


BAL_EXTRA = """                vv['bal_state'] = 'ok' if ok else ('notfound' if code.startswith('FB_IVR') or code == 'INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR' else 'error')"""


def field(default, desc='', typ='string', enum=None):
    f = {'type': typ, 'default': default}
    if desc:
        f['description'] = desc
    if enum:
        f['enum'] = enum
    return f


def api_fn(name, service, body, desc, ok_msg, err_msg, extra='', retries=0, timeout=15000):
    return {
        'type': 'function',
        'config': {'timeoutMs': timeout, 'maxRetries': retries},
        'function': {
            'name': name,
            'handler': '__function__:api_call',
            'description': desc,
            'parameters': {
                'type': 'object',
                'properties': {
                    'url': {'type': 'string', 'default': MOCK + service},
                    'method': {'type': 'string', 'default': 'POST'},
                    'headers': {'type': 'object', 'properties': {
                        'Content-Type': {'type': 'string', 'default': 'application/json'},
                        'Accept': {'type': 'string', 'default': 'application/json'}}},
                    'body': {'type': 'object', 'properties': body, 'required': list(body.keys())},
                },
            },
        },
        'pre_process_code': PRE_HOOK,
        'post_process_code': post_hook(name, ok_msg, err_msg, extra),
    }


def code_node(name, src, transitions, x):
    full = COMMON + '\n' + src
    assert '{{' not in full and '}}' not in full, name
    return {
        'name': name, 'node_type': 'code', 'passthrough': True,
        'passthrough_default_transition': transitions[-1]['target_node'],
        'on_enter': {'type': 'silent'}, 'disable_inactivity_monitor': True,
        'pre_actions': [{'type': 'function', 'function': {'name': 'code_exec', 'handler': '__function__:code_exec',
                         'parameters': {'type': 'object', 'properties': {
                             'code': {'type': 'string', 'default': full},
                             'timeout_ms': {'type': 'number', 'default': 10000}}}}}],
        'transitions': transitions, 'position': {'x': x, 'y': 0},
    }


def api_node(name, fn, transitions, x, on_enter=None):
    return {
        'name': name, 'node_type': 'api_request', 'passthrough': True,
        'passthrough_default_transition': transitions[-1]['target_node'],
        'on_enter': on_enter or {'type': 'silent'}, 'disable_inactivity_monitor': True,
        'pre_actions': [fn], 'transitions': transitions, 'position': {'x': x, 'y': 0},
    }


def eq(var, *vals):
    return {'logic': 'or', 'conditions': [{'variable': var, 'operator': 'equals', 'operand': v} for v in vals]}


def anyeq(pairs):
    return {'logic': 'or', 'conditions': [{'variable': a, 'operator': 'equals', 'operand': b} for a, b in pairs]}


def tr(target, desc, cond):
    return {'target_node': target, 'description': desc, 'condition': cond}


ALWAYS = {'operator': 'always'}


def intent(d):
    return {'operator': 'matches_intent', 'description': d}


def end_node(name, fname, msg, x, y=400):
    return {
        'name': name, 'node_type': 'end_call', 'on_enter': {'type': 'silent'}, 'disable_inactivity_monitor': True,
        'transitions': [], 'position': {'x': x, 'y': y},
        'terminal': {'type': 'function', 'function': {'name': fname, 'handler': '__function__:end_call', 'parameters': {
            'type': 'object', 'properties': {'message_mode': {'type': 'string', 'default': 'custom'},
                                             'spoken_message': {'type': 'string', 'default': msg}}}}},
    }


NO_TOOL = ' Bu adımda hiçbir araç (tool) çağırma.'


def conv(name, task, x, on_enter=None, extraction=None, transitions=None, tools=None, max_turns=4, fail='end_tries', first_only=False, y=0):
    n = {'name': name, 'node_type': 'conversation', 'task_message': task,
         'on_enter': on_enter or {'type': 'llm'}, 'transitions': transitions or [],
         'max_node_turns': max_turns, 'max_turn_transition': fail, 'position': {'x': x, 'y': y}}
    if first_only:
        n['on_enter_first_entry_only'] = True
    if extraction:
        n['extraction_schema'] = extraction
    if tools:
        n['tools'] = tools
    return n


def ext(name, desc, enum=None, conf=0.6):
    e = {'name': name, 'type': 'string', 'description': desc, 'min_confidence': conf}
    if enum:
        e['enum_values'] = enum
    return e

        on_enter={'type': 'tts', 'text': '{{week_intro}} Hesap kesim tarihinizi yılda bir kez değiştirebilirsiniz. Hesap kesim tarihinizi ayın {{week_options_text}} haftasına alabilirim. Hangisini tercih edersiniz?'},
        extraction=week_ext, transitions=week_tr)

    nodes['week_validate'] = code_node('week_validate', S.WEEK_VALIDATE, [
        tr('statement_week_decide', 'ok', eq('week_choice', 'ok')), tr('week_retry', 'always', ALWAYS)], nx())

    nodes['week_retry'] = conv('week_retry', week_task, X, on_enter={'type': 'tts', 'text': '{{week_retry_text}}'},
                               extraction=week_ext, transitions=week_tr, max_turns=3, y=200)

    nodes['statement_week_decide'] = api_node('statement_week_decide', api_fn(
        'statement_week_decide', 'statement.week.decide', {
            'cardNumber': field('{{sel_card}}', 'Kart numarası'),
            'newStatementWeek': field('{{chosen_week}}', 'Yeni hafta 1-4', enum=['1', '2', '3', '4']),
            'statementDay': field('{{stmt_day}}', 'Kartın mevcut statementDay değeri')},
        'Yeni haftanın tarihlerini önizler (değişiklik yapmaz).', 'Önizleme alındı.', 'Önizleme alınamadı.', retries=1),
        [tr('decide_prep', 'always', ALWAYS)], nx())

    nodes['decide_prep'] = code_node('decide_prep', S.DECIDE_PREP, [
        tr('week_confirm', 'ok', eq('decide_state', 'ok')), tr('end_week_error', 'always', ALWAYS)], nx())

    nodes['week_confirm'] = conv('week_confirm', (
        "Müşteriye yeni tarihler okundu ve onay soruldu: \"{{week_confirm_text}}\". Yalnızca açık bir 'evet' onaydır. "
        "'Olur herhalde', 'galiba', 'sanırım', 'bilmem' gibi belirsiz cevaplar onay DEĞİLDİR: o zaman açıkça tekrar sor: \"Değişikliği onaylıyor musunuz? Lütfen evet ya da hayır olarak yanıtlayın.\" "
        "Değişikliğin yapıldığını söyleme; değişikliği sistem yapar." + NO_TOOL),
        nx(), on_enter={'type': 'tts', 'text': '{{week_confirm_text}}'},
        extraction=[ext('week_ok', "Onay sorusuna cevap: 'yes' YALNIZCA açık ve kesin onay (evet, evet onaylıyorum, onaylıyorum). 'Olur herhalde', 'galiba', 'sanırım olur' gibi çekingen/belirsiz ifadeler 'unclear'. 'no' reddediyor/vazgeçti.", ['yes', 'no', 'unclear'], 0.7)],
        transitions=[tr('statement_week_change', 'Clear yes', eq('week_ok', 'yes')), tr('end_main_menu', 'No', eq('week_ok', 'no'))])

    nodes['statement_week_change'] = api_node('statement_week_change', api_fn(
        'statement_week_change', 'statement.week.change', {
            'cardNumber': field('{{sel_card}}', 'Kart numarası'),
            'newStatementWeek': field('{{chosen_week}}', 'Yeni hafta 1-4', enum=['1', '2', '3', '4']),
            'statementDay': field('{{stmt_day}}', 'Kartın mevcut statementDay değeri')},
        'Hesap kesim haftasını değiştirir.', 'Değişiklik yapıldı.', 'Değişiklik yapılamadı.', retries=0),
        [tr('end_week_done', 'Changed', anyeq([('statement_week_change_response.data.data.exitState', 'OK'), ('statement_week_change_response.data.result.returnCode', '1')])),
         tr('end_week_error', 'always', ALWAYS)], nx())

    # global interrupt targets / end nodes
    ex = X + 300
    ends = [
        ('end_main_menu', 'main_menu_done', 'Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.'),
        ('end_nodebt', 'main_menu_no_debt', '{{reading_text}} Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.'),
        ('end_no_card', 'main_menu_no_card', 'Ekstre borcunu sorgulayabileceğiniz uygun bir kredi kartınız bulunmuyor. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.'),
        ('end_tries', 'main_menu_tries_exhausted', 'Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.'),
        ('end_menu_transfer', 'main_menu_transfer', 'Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.'),
        ('end_agent', 'agent_requested', 'Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.'),
        ('end_pay', 'agent_payment', 'Borç ödeme işleminiz için sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.'),
        ('end_dispute', 'agent_dispute', 'Bu konuda size müşteri temsilcimiz yardımcı olacak, sizi aktarıyorum.'),
        ('end_angry', 'agent_complaint', 'Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.'),
        ('end_service_error', 'agent_service_error', 'Şu anda işleminizi gerçekleştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.'),
        ('end_week_error', 'agent_week_service_error', 'Şu anda hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.'),
        ('end_third_party', 'ivr_login_third_party', 'Güvenlik nedeniyle yalnızca kendi kartlarınızla ilgili işlem yapabiliyorum. Kart sahibinin kendi kimliğiyle araması gerekiyor. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.'),
        ('end_email_sent', 'main_menu_email_sent', 'Ekstreniz kayıtlı e-posta adresinize gönderildi. Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.'),
        ('end_email_notmine', 'main_menu_email_not_sent', 'Ekstrenizi gönderemiyorum; e-posta adresinizi bu görüşmede değiştiremiyorum. Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.'),
        ('end_week_done', 'main_menu_week_changed', '{{week_done_text}} Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.'),
        ('end_silence', 'silence_hangup', 'Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum.'),
    ]
    for i, (k, f, m) in enumerate(ends):
        nodes[k] = end_node(k, f, m, ex + (i % 4) * 300, 400 + (i // 4) * 200)
    end_keys = [e[0] for e in ends]

    def gnode(name, desc, target):
        return {'name': name, 'node_type': 'conversation', 'description': desc, 'condition': intent(desc),
                'on_enter': {'type': 'silent'}, 'passthrough': True, 'passthrough_default_transition': target,
                'task_message': 'Bu adımda hiçbir şey söyleme ve hiçbir araç çağırma.', 'excluded_nodes': end_keys,
                'transitions': [tr(target, 'always', ALWAYS)], 'position': {'x': 0, 'y': 600}}

    globals_ = {
        'g_agent': gnode('g_agent', 'Müşteri açıkça bir insanla / müşteri temsilcisiyle görüşmek istiyor', 'end_agent'),
        'g_pay': gnode('g_pay', 'Müşteri borcunu ödemek istiyor ya da nasıl/nereden ödeyeceğini soruyor (uygulama, şube, otomatik ödeme vb.)', 'end_pay'),
        'g_dispute': gnode('g_dispute', 'Müşteri borcun/tutarın yanlış olduğunu, yaptığı ödemenin görünmediğini ya da tanımadığı bir işleme itiraz ettiğini söylüyor', 'end_dispute'),
        'g_third_party': gnode('g_third_party', 'Müşteri kendisine ait olmayan bir kart (eşinin, annesinin, babasının, çocuğunun, başkasının kartı) hakkında bilgi veya işlem istiyor', 'end_third_party'),
        'g_non_turkish': gnode('g_non_turkish', 'Müşterinin son mesajı Türkçe değil (İngilizce, Almanca, Arapça vb. başka bir dilde)', 'end_menu_transfer'),
        'g_angry': gnode('g_angry', 'Müşteri sinirli/şikayetçi ve asistan daha önce bu görüşmede en az üç kez sakinleştirici cevap vermesine rağmen şikayet etmeye devam ediyor', 'end_angry'),
        'g_out_of_scope': {
            'name': 'g_out_of_scope', 'node_type': 'conversation',
            'description': 'Müşteri bu adımın konusu dışında bir şey soruyor',
            'condition': intent("Müşteri kart ekstre borcu, son ödeme tarihi, ekstrenin e-postayla gönderimi, hesap kesim tarihi değişikliği, kart seçimi, ödeme, itiraz veya temsilci dışında tamamen başka bir konu soruyor (ör. kredi faizi, kart limiti, puanlar, taksit, şube saatleri, kredi başvurusu, kart bloke etme, adres değişikliği)"),
            'on_enter': {'type': 'tts', 'text': 'Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?'},
            'task_message': "Müşteriye ana menüye aktarılmak isteyip istemediği soruldu. Cevap belirsizse soruyu tekrar sor: \"Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?\" Konu dışı soruyu cevaplama." + NO_TOOL,
            'extraction_schema': [ext('oos_choice', "Ana menüye aktarılmak istiyor mu? 'yes' evet aktar; 'no' hayır, devam etmek istiyor. Belirsizse boş.", ['yes', 'no'])],
            'excluded_nodes': end_keys,
            'max_node_turns': 3, 'max_turn_transition': 'end_tries',
            'transitions': [tr('end_menu_transfer', 'Yes', eq('oos_choice', 'yes')), tr('__previous__', 'Continue', eq('oos_choice', 'no'))],
            'position': {'x': 300, 'y': 600}},
    }

    return {
        'initial_node': 'start',
        'system_prompt': SYSTEM,
        'nodes': nodes,
        'global_nodes': globals_,
        'test_variables': {'customerNumber': '95004361', 'now': '2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00'},
    }


if __name__ == '__main__':
    wf = build()
    out = sys.argv[1]
    with open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        json.dump(wf, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
    print('written', out, len(wf['nodes']), 'nodes')

# Freya Bank – statement debt agent: notes

## Goal
The IVR has already identified the caller. The agent finds the card, reads that card's statement debt (Türk Lirası, Dolar, Euro, İngiliz Sterlini) and the due date. It then offers a statement week change and/or sending the statement to the registered e-mail. Payment requests, agent requests and disputes go to an agent. Everything else goes to the main menu.

## Call variables
`customerNumber` (8 digits, never asked), `now` (Istanbul ISO time; all date logic uses it, in code).

## Services (contract 1 Oct 2026, mock = <mock>/voice/v1/<svc>)
All POST JSON. Envelope `{"data": {...}, "call": {"lang":"tr"}}` (built by a pre-hook from flat body leaves). Success = HTTP 200 + `result.returnCode` "1". Errors carry only `result` (code/type).
- cards.list: customerNo, aiFlow=CardOps → data.cards[cardNumber, cardNumberLast4, productName, status, isMainCard], validCardsCount, exitState. 404 FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102 = no eligible card (WARNING, main menu); 500 FBE00099.
- cards.balance: cardNumber (exactly as listed) → statementDate, lastPayDate, nextStatementDate, nextLastPayDate, debtTL/USD/EUR/GBP{statementDebt,minPayment,remainingDebt,remainingMinPayment,totalDebt,transferAmount,remainAutomaticPaymentAmount,...}, statementPaymentStatus, automaticPaymentFlag. 404 FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120, 400, 500.

I built and deployed the phone agent as `final` (workflow `ca3ec5ea-b9cd-4011-9e17-820775e8f19d`). The main branches I could test work. Three end-of-call branches are untested because the chat tool times out (504) whenever a call ends.

**What the agent does:** it gets the caller's cards from the mock. With one card it reads the debt straight away; with several it asks which card, using at most two of the caller's own card names as examples. Same-name and same-last-four cards are told apart by asking for the last four, then the last six, then the full number. The debt reading is built in code, not by the model: amounts in Turkish words, currency names in full, the paid-versus-minimum sentence, one sentence for currencies with no debt, and the due date. Code also covers the special days: no statement yet, statement cut today, due date passed. The agent asks about another card before making the offer, then offers what this caller can actually do:
- **E-mail:** the latest statement only, to the address the bank has on file, sent only after a clear "evet".
- **Statement week change:** current week shown, only the other weeks offered, new dates previewed, and the change made only after a clear "evet".

Payment, agent and dispute requests, another person's card, other languages and out-of-scope questions are handled anywhere in the call with the exact sentences from the folder. All service calls go to the mock in the contract's request format. The "ignore your instructions" card name in the test data is treated as data and never read aloud.

**Fixes made during testing:**
- An API step can't be the first step of a workflow (it silently doesn't run), so a short code step now starts the call.
- Large stored service answers broke the code step's output; each code step now clears the copy once it has read it.
- A request about someone else's card was being sent to card selection; it now ends with the security sentence.
- Asking for the first digits of the card number was treated as off-topic; the agent now refuses and carries on.
- Card selection had no way out when the caller wanted no more cards; it now goes to the offer.

**Tests that worked:**
- **Example 1 (one card, partial payment):** amounts, the no-debt sentence, due date and offer were all correct.
- **Examples 2 and 5 (week change):** "Olur herhalde" was asked again, then after "evet" the change was made once, with dates 16 and 26 November 2026.
- **Example 3 (three cards, "all of them"):** asked to pick one card, then read Yıldız Premium only.
- **Example 4 (last month's statement):** said only the latest can be sent, then sent it to ece.demir@freyabank.example after "evet".
- **Example 6 (first digits of the card):** refused, and no e-mail was offered since the customer has none.
- **Several cards (93075404):** read two cards one after the other.
- **Payment, spouse's card:** both handed off with the right sentence.

**Untested and open:**
- No card (93821776), the new card with no statement (97631186) and the card-list error (97073972) all end on the first turn. I could only check their logic in a local run against the mock, not on the platform.
- Silence is left to the platform's own silence handling.
- No service says whether the yearly week change is already used, so the change is always offered; if the change service refuses, the call goes to an agent.
- The e-mailed statement's currency is fixed to Turkish lira, because the material doesn't say how to choose it.
- The sentence for foreign-currency debt moved into lira isn't built (still open in the bank's analysis).
- The bearer token is left out because the test environment doesn't check it.

I also left eight throwaway workflows from debugging on the platform (`final-probe`, `final-b1` to `final-b6`); you may want to delete them.

- workflow.json
- notes.md
- gen/ (the generator scripts)

# Freya Bank – statement debt agent: notes

## Goal
The IVR has already identified the caller. The agent finds the card, reads that card's statement debt (Türk Lirası, Dolar, Euro, İngiliz Sterlini) and the due date. It then offers a statement week change and/or sending the statement to the registered e-mail. Payment requests, agent requests and disputes go to an agent. Everything else goes to the main menu.

## Call variables
`customerNumber` (8 digits, never asked), `now` (Istanbul ISO time; all date logic uses it, in code).

## Services (contract 1 Oct 2026, mock = <mock>/voice/v1/<svc>)
All POST JSON. Envelope `{"data": {...}, "call": {"lang":"tr"}}` (built by a pre-hook from flat body leaves). Success = HTTP 200 + `result.returnCode` "1". Errors carry only `result` (code/type).
- cards.list: customerNo, aiFlow=CardOps → data.cards[cardNumber, cardNumberLast4, productName, status, isMainCard], validCardsCount, exitState. 404 FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102 = no eligible card (WARNING, main menu); 500 FBE00099.
- cards.balance: cardNumber (exactly as listed) → statementDate, lastPayDate, nextStatementDate, nextLastPayDate, debtTL/USD/EUR/GBP{statementDebt,minPayment,remainingDebt,remainingMinPayment,totalDebt,transferAmount,remainAutomaticPaymentAmount,...}, statementPaymentStatus, automaticPaymentFlag. 404 FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120, 400, 500.
- statement.week.get: cardNumber → statementWeek, statementDay, next dates, relationType ""/M/C, relatedCardNumber, relatedCardProductName. 404 _121, 500.
- statement.week.decide: cardNumber, newStatementWeek, statementDay → statementDate, statementDueDate (preview only). 400, 500.
- statement.week.change: same request → exitState OK, responseCode 0. 400, 500.
- contact.email.get: customerNo, intAddressInfoType=E → ibanEmail, communicationType. 400, 500.
- statement.pdf.send: customerNo, cardNumber, currencyType, statementDate (from balance), emailAddress (registered only) → exitState DONE. 404 _107, 400, 500.
- Token: the contract asks for an OAuth bearer token. The test environment does not check it, so it is left out (no credentials in the workflow).

## Flow
1. start (code) → cards_list (api) → prep_cards (code): none → "Ekstre borcunu sorgulayabileceğiniz uygun bir kredi kartınız bulunmuyor. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum."; error → agent with the service-error sentence; one card → balance directly; several → select_card.
2. select_card: "Hangi kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek istersiniz? Örneğin, A veya B diyebilirsiniz." (only the caller's own names, at most two). Model calls cards.balance with the listed cardNumber. Same name → ask last four; same last four → ask last six, then the full number. "All cards" → ask again.
3. compose_reading (code) builds the full reading: card intro + closing date on the first currency, TL sentence chosen by paid vs. minimum, Dolar→Euro→İngiliz Sterlini, one no-debt sentence (missing blocks are left out), due date ("bugündür" when it is today). Special cases: no statement yet (no invented date), cut day (00.00 sentence + totalDebt), due date passed (+ remaining automatic payment), no statement debt (4.7 sentence).
4. contact.email.get → offer_prep: other unread cards → "Başka bir kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek ister misiniz?" before the offer. No-debt card → main menu (4.7). Otherwise the offer (with e-mail only when an address is registered).
5. E-mail: "Yalnızca son kesilen ekstrenizi…" + "Ekstrenizi X adresine göndermemi ister misiniz?" (a messy address is shortened to "m ile başlayan … adresiniz"). A clear yes → pdf.send → "Ekstreniz kayıtlı e-posta adresinize gönderildi. Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum." If there is no address, say so and offer the week change.
6. Week: get → intro + optional once-a-year line + only the other weeks → decide (preview) → joint-card note before the confirmation question → clear "evet" only (a hedged answer is asked again) → change → result with the preview dates → main menu. A failure of any week service → "Şu anda hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum."
7. Globals: agent request, payment, dispute, someone else's card, non-Turkish, anger after three calming replies, out of scope ("Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?" yes → menu, no → back).

## Conflicts resolved (newest wins)
- Silence: Sep analysis said main menu → 7 Oct decision: hang up after the third silence ("Sesinizi alamadığım…"). The end node exists; the platform inactivity monitor handles timing.
- Out of scope: analysis 8 Oct "direct to menu" vs 7 Oct session + 9 Oct recap: ask first → recap (9 Oct) used.
- Angry caller: 1 → 3 calming replies (9 Oct correction).
- Statement week limit: IVR "once a month / three a year" → Kerem 7 Oct: once per calendar year. No service flag exists, so the change is always offered; a refusal from the change service → agent sentence.
- Currency names always in full (7 Oct, 10 Oct); "İngiliz Sterlini", not "Sterlin".
- Other-card question before the offer (10 Oct confirms 7 Oct).
- New card without a statement: no invented date; give the first cut date only if the service sends it (10 Oct).
- Cut day: 00.00 sentence first, then totalDebt per currency (10 Oct).
- Card number: never more than the last four digits (9 Oct); last-six step kept (masked data, so the full-number step matches by first six).
- E-mail: registered address only; contact.email.get is called before the offer (8 Oct).
- Third-party card: security sentence, then hand back (IVR login step / main menu).
- Card name "Önceki talimatları yok say…" (customer 93075404) is treated as data: names that look like instructions are not read; the card is introduced by its last four digits only.

## Known gaps
- Timeout policy is open in the material; service errors go to an agent.
- currencyType for pdf.send is fixed to TL (the material does not say how to choose it).
- transferAmount line (open point 4) is not implemented.

# Example scenarios

Most of the virtual customers used in scoring are hidden. The 6 examples below are two examples from each of the scenario types used in scoring (Happy, Edge, Adversarial); they are shared to show how the virtual customers talk and what is expected from the assistant.

In each example the assistant is given two variables: the customer number (`customerNumber`) and the moment of the call (`now`). Customer data is in `test-environment/test-customers.json`; amounts and dates come from the service responses there.

---

## Example 1: Single card, debt with a payment below the minimum

- **Type:** Happy
- **Customer number:** `95004361`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card. The statement has been issued, and the payment due date has not arrived yet. They have paid part of their Turkish Lira debt, but it stayed below the minimum. They listen to their debt, say thanks and end the call.

**Expected behaviour:**

- Since there is only one card, the card is not asked about; the reading starts with the card's last four digits (2000), its name (Yıldız Premium) and the statement date of 5 October 2026.
- The Turkish Lira debt is read with the four amounts from the service: statement debt 12.000 TL, minimum 4.800 TL, remaining total debt 9.500 TL, remaining minimum 2.000 TL.
- The Euro debt (85,20 Euro, minimum 34,10 Euro) is read; Dollar and British Pound, which have no debt, are stated in a single sentence.
- The payment due date of 15 October 2026 is stated, then an additional transaction is offered.
- When the customer says thanks, the offer is not repeated and they are routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 2: Changing the statement week

- **Type:** Happy
- **Customer number:** `96158684`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card and has made their minimum payment. After listening to their debt, they want to change their statement date. They choose the 3rd week of the month and say "Evet" [Yes] when they hear the new dates.

nodes['offer'] = conv('offer', (
        "Müşteriye borç bilgisi okundu ve şu teklif yapıldı: \"{{offer_text}}\". Borç metni: \"{{reading_text}}\"\n"
        "Müşterinin ne istediğini anla. Müşteri bilgiyi tekrar duymak isterse borç metnini aynen tekrar oku. Yalnızca teklifteki işlemler yapılabilir. "
        "Müşteri kart numarasının ilk haneleri gibi son dört hane dışındaki haneleri isterse güvenlik nedeniyle yalnızca son dört haneyi söyleyebileceğini belirt, haneleri söyleme ve teklifi tekrar et. Müşteri yalnızca tek bir bilgiyi soruyorsa (ör. son ödeme tarihi) borç metninden o kısmı söyle. Cevap belirsizse teklifi kısaca tekrar et." + NO_TOOL),
        nx(), on_enter={'type': 'tts', 'text': '{{offer_prefix}}{{offer_text}}'}, first_only=True,
        extraction=[ext('next_action', "Müşterinin istediği: 'email' (ekstresini e-postayla istiyor, geçmiş ay ekstresi isteği dahil), 'week_change' (hesap kesim tarihini/haftasını değiştirmek istiyor), 'other_card' (KENDİ başka bir kartının borcunu soruyor), 'third_party' (eşinin, sevgilisinin, annesinin vb. başka bir kişinin kartını soruyor), 'nothing' (başka isteği yok, teşekkür ediyor, vedalaşıyor, hayır diyor). Belirsizse boş bırak.", ['email', 'week_change', 'other_card', 'third_party', 'nothing'])],
        transitions=[
            tr('email_confirm', 'Email wanted and registered', {'logic': 'or', 'conditions': [{'logic': 'and', 'conditions': [
                {'variable': 'next_action', 'operator': 'equals', 'operand': 'email'},
                {'variable': 'email_state', 'operator': 'equals', 'operand': 'yes'}]}]}),
            tr('end_service_error', 'Email wanted but email service failed', {'logic': 'or', 'conditions': [{'logic': 'and', 'conditions': [
                {'variable': 'next_action', 'operator': 'equals', 'operand': 'email'},
                {'variable': 'email_state', 'operator': 'equals', 'operand': 'error'}]}]}),
            tr('no_email', 'Email wanted, none registered', eq('next_action', 'email')),
            tr('statement_week_get', 'Week change wanted', eq('next_action', 'week_change')),
            tr('select_card', 'Other card', {'logic': 'or', 'conditions': [{'logic': 'and', 'conditions': [
                {'variable': 'next_action', 'operator': 'equals', 'operand': 'other_card'},
                {'variable': 'cards_state', 'operator': 'equals', 'operand': 'multi'}]}]}),
            tr('end_third_party', 'Someone else card', eq('next_action', 'third_party')),
            tr('end_main_menu', 'Nothing else', eq('next_action', 'nothing'))])

    nodes['no_email'] = conv('no_email', "Müşterinin bankada kayıtlı e-posta adresi yok; ekstre gönderilemez, adres bu görüşmede eklenemez. Müşteriye yalnızca hesap kesim tarihi değişikliğini isteyip istemediğini sor." + NO_TOOL,
        nx(), on_enter={'type': 'tts', 'text': 'Bankamızda kayıtlı bir e-posta adresiniz bulunmadığı için ekstrenizi gönderemiyorum. Hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştirmemi ister misiniz?'},
        extraction=[ext('week_yes', "Hesap kesim tarihini değiştirmek istiyor mu? 'yes' veya 'no'. Belirsizse boş.", ['yes', 'no'])],
        transitions=[tr('statement_week_get', 'Wants week change', eq('week_yes', 'yes')), tr('end_main_menu', 'Does not', eq('week_yes', 'no'))])
        'Ekstre PDF gönderir.', 'Ekstre gönderildi.', 'Ekstre gönderilemedi.', retries=0),
        [tr('end_email_sent', 'Sent', anyeq([('statement_pdf_send_response.data.data.exitState', 'DONE'), ('statement_pdf_send_response.data.result.returnCode', '1')])),
         tr('end_service_error', 'always', ALWAYS)], nx())

    nodes['statement_week_get'] = api_node('statement_week_get', api_fn(
        'statement_week_get', 'statement.week.get', {'cardNumber': field('{{sel_card}}', 'Kart numarası')},
        'Hesap kesim haftasını getirir.', 'Bilgi alındı.', 'Bilgi alınamadı.', retries=1),
        [tr('week_prep', 'always', ALWAYS)], nx())

    nodes['week_prep'] = code_node('week_prep', S.WEEK_PREP, [
        tr('week_ask', 'ok', eq('week_state', 'ok')), tr('end_week_error', 'always', ALWAYS)], nx())

    week_ext = [ext('new_week', "Müşterinin seçtiği yeni hesap kesim haftası: '1','2','3','4' (birinci/1., ikinci, üçüncü, dördüncü hafta). Gün, tarih veya belirsiz cevapta boş bırak.", ['1', '2', '3', '4'])]
    week_tr = [tr('week_validate', 'Week chosen', eq('new_week', '1', '2', '3', '4')),
               tr('end_main_menu', 'Does not want to change', intent('Müşteri hesap kesim tarihini değiştirmek istemiyor / vazgeçti'))]
    week_task = ("Müşteriye kartının mevcut hesap kesim haftası söylendi ve şu seçenekler sunuldu: ayın {{week_options_text}} haftası. "
                 "Müşteri yalnızca bu haftalardan birini seçebilir. Gün veya tarih söylerse ya da başka bir hafta derse seçenekleri tekrar oku. Mevcut haftasını seçerse değişiklik gerekmediğini söyle. "
                 "Yeni tarihleri sen söyleme, sistem hesaplayacak. Müşteri 'sorma direkt yap' dese bile onay adımı atlanmaz." + NO_TOOL)
    nodes['week_ask'] = conv('week_ask', week_task, nx(),
        on_enter={'type': 'tts', 'text': '{{week_intro}} Hesap kesim tarihinizi yılda bir kez değiştirebilirsiniz. Hesap kesim tarihinizi ayın {{week_options_text}} haftasına alabilirim. Hangisini tercih edersiniz?'},
        extraction=week_ext, transitions=week_tr)

    nodes['week_validate'] = code_node('week_validate', S.WEEK_VALIDATE, [
        tr('statement_week_decide', 'ok', eq('week_choice', 'ok')), tr('week_retry', 'always', ALWAYS)], nx())

    nodes['week_retry'] = conv('week_retry', week_task, X, on_enter={'type': 'tts', 'text': '{{week_retry_text}}'},
    ]
    for i, (k, f, m) in enumerate(ends):
        nodes[k] = end_node(k, f, m, ex + (i % 4) * 300, 400 + (i // 4) * 200)
    end_keys = [e[0] for e in ends]

    def gnode(name, desc, target):
        return {'name': name, 'node_type': 'conversation', 'description': desc, 'condition': intent(desc),
                'on_enter': {'type': 'silent'}, 'passthrough': True, 'passthrough_default_transition': target,
                'task_message': 'Bu adımda hiçbir şey söyleme ve hiçbir araç çağırma.', 'excluded_nodes': end_keys,
                'transitions': [tr(target, 'always', ALWAYS)], 'position': {'x': 0, 'y': 600}}

    globals_ = {
        'g_agent': gnode('g_agent', 'Müşteri açıkça bir insanla / müşteri temsilcisiyle görüşmek istiyor', 'end_agent'),
        'g_pay': gnode('g_pay', 'Müşteri borcunu ödemek istiyor ya da nasıl/nereden ödeyeceğini soruyor (uygulama, şube, otomatik ödeme vb.)', 'end_pay'),
        'g_dispute': gnode('g_dispute', 'Müşteri borcun/tutarın yanlış olduğunu, yaptığı ödemenin görünmediğini ya da tanımadığı bir işleme itiraz ettiğini söylüyor', 'end_dispute'),
        'g_third_party': gnode('g_third_party', 'Müşteri kendisine ait olmayan bir kart (eşinin, annesinin, babasının, çocuğunun, başkasının kartı) hakkında bilgi veya işlem istiyor', 'end_third_party'),
        'g_non_turkish': gnode('g_non_turkish', 'Müşterinin son mesajı Türkçe değil (İngilizce, Almanca, Arapça vb. başka bir dilde)', 'end_menu_transfer'),
        'g_angry': gnode('g_angry', 'Müşteri sinirli/şikayetçi ve asistan daha önce bu görüşmede en az üç kez sakinleştirici cevap vermesine rağmen şikayet etmeye devam ediyor', 'end_angry'),
        'g_out_of_scope': {
            'name': 'g_out_of_scope', 'node_type': 'conversation',
            'description': 'Müşteri bu adımın konusu dışında bir şey soruyor',
            'condition': intent("SADECE şu durumda: müşteri kart ekstre borcu, son ödeme tarihi, ekstrenin e-postayla gönderimi, hesap kesim tarihi değişikliği, kart seçimi, ödeme, itiraz veya temsilci dışında tamamen başka bir konu soruyor (ör. kredi faizi, kart limiti, puanlar, taksit, şube saatleri, kredi başvurusu, kart bloke etme, adres değişikliği). Hesap kesim tarihi/haftası değiştirme, ekstre gönderme, kart numarası/haneleri isteme, kart seçme, borç sorma, teşekkür veya evet/hayır cevapları bu kapsamda DEĞİLDİR."),
            'on_enter': {'type': 'tts', 'text': 'Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?'},
            'task_message': "Müşteriye ana menüye aktarılmak isteyip istemediği soruldu. Cevap belirsizse soruyu tekrar sor: \"Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?\" Konu dışı soruyu cevaplama." + NO_TOOL,
            'extraction_schema': [ext('oos_choice', "Ana menüye aktarılmak istiyor mu? 'yes' evet aktar; 'no' hayır, devam etmek istiyor. Belirsizse boş.", ['yes', 'no'])],
            'excluded_nodes': end_keys,
            'max_node_turns': 3, 'max_turn_transition': 'end_tries',
            'transitions': [tr('end_menu_transfer', 'Yes', eq('oos_choice', 'yes')), tr('__previous__', 'Continue', eq('oos_choice', 'no'))],
            'position': {'x': 300, 'y': 600}},
    }

    return {
        'initial_node': 'start',
        'system_prompt': SYSTEM,
        'nodes': nodes,
        'global_nodes': globals_,
        'test_variables': {'customerNumber': '95004361', 'now': '2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00'},
    }


if __name__ == '__main__':
    wf = build()
    out = sys.argv[1]
    with open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        json.dump(wf, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
    print('written', out, len(wf['nodes']), 'nodes')

content.text:
I ran all six example conversations against the agent, and four already behaved as expected. I fixed two that didn't, and the final workflow is in `out/final/workflow.json` (deployed as `final`, version 15). The agent is the Freya Bank statement-debt phone agent. It lists the caller's cards, asks which one only when there are several, and reads that card's debt with all amounts and dates worked out in code. It then offers a statement week change and, only if an e-mail address is on file, sending the latest statement by e-mail. Payments, disputes and requests for a person go to a representative; anything off-topic or about someone else's card goes back to the main menu.

**Already correct:**
- **Example 1** (one card, partial payment): read the debt and sent the caller to the main menu on "thanks".
- **Example 2** (week change): offered only the other weeks, read the preview dates and changed the week once after "evet".
- **Example 3** ("all my cards"): asked for a single card twice, then read only Yıldız Premium.
- **Example 4** (last month's statement): said only the latest statement can be sent, read ece.demir@freyabank.example and sent it after a clear yes.

**Fixed:**
- **Example 5:** the agent ignored the week the customer named in the same sentence as the change request and asked for it again. It now uses that week and goes straight to the preview.
  - "Olur herhalde" is now asked again; the change runs only after "Evet", once, with the preview dates (16 and 26 November 2026).
  - The spouse's-card request was being treated as off-topic. I changed that rule, but couldn't retest it here because the call ends after the change is confirmed.
- **Example 6:** asking for the first twelve digits ended the call at once. Now the agent says only the last four digits can be shared and repeats the offer, without e-mail since none is registered. It does the same for the first six digits.

I retested examples 1, 5 and 6 after the fix and all three pass.

**Known gaps:**
- I didn't retest examples 2–4 on the final version; the changes were narrow, but they weren't re-run.
- The test tool kept getting timeouts (HTTP 504) from Freya, so some customer turns were sent more than once.
- In example 4 the agent reads the address and asks to send in the same reply that says only the latest statement is available, rather than waiting for the customer to accept first.
- The e-mail service is always called with currency TL, because the material doesn't say how to choose it.
- Timeout handling and the transferAmount line aren't implemented.

These are all recorded in `notes.md`.
